title: Medicaid expansion can spill into participation in other safety-net programs
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 26504 and Census CES Working Paper 26-32, using border-county and restricted-ACS comparisons of ACA Medicaid expansion and other program participation
geography: United States; contiguous county pairs crossing state borders and restricted-access ACS adults ages 25–64, with county administrative outcomes through 2016 and ACS outcomes through 2017

observations.period: 2010–2017 ACA Medicaid expansion; SNAP, TANF, and EITC participation

denominator.unit: contiguous county pairs crossing state borders that differed in Medicaid expansion status in 2014; the broader 2010–2016 discordant-pair analysis uses 746 pairs

SNAP_participation.value: about 0.6 additional participants per 100 people for a 0-to-138% income-limit increase; 0.49 percentage points in the restricted ACS

TANF_participation.value: increased, especially among single parents; about 0.49 percentage points from a 100-percentage-point income-limit increase in the ACS estimate

EITC_participation.value: possibly increased; preferred border-pair estimate is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero

insurance.value: a typical 0-to-138% expansion reduced uninsurance by about 2.2 percentage points

application_cost.value: information or transaction-cost spillovers are the leading interpretation, not a fully observed household mechanism

observations.method: Contiguous county-pair border design with county-pair-by-year fixed effects for administrative EITC/SNAP measures, plus restricted-access ACS individual participation comparisons and state policy-environment heterogeneity.
observations.uncertainty: The evidence is quasi-experimental and program-specific precision differs. County-level SNAP data omit states that report only at the state level. The ACS is a repeated cross-section rather than a panel following one household through enrollment and later wellbeing. The record does not establish benefit adequacy, food security, household adaptation, trust, action, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: People and households in expansion/non-expansion border comparisons; ACS participation conditional on eligibility.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cross-program participation may reflect information, transaction costs, labor supply, local implementation, or other expansion-linked changes; the same household route is not observed.

related_sources.claim: Earlier NBER version of the Medicaid-expansion spillover research line; not treated as an independent replication.
Official Census CES paper with the detailed border-pair, ACS, subgroup, and mechanism estimates.

boundary: The study closes a Medicaid-eligibility to other-program-participation arrow and sharpens its size and subgroup pattern. It does not close notice, application completion for a named household, benefit amount, adequacy, food security, trust, political action, or recovery; the Census and NBER versions are one research line rather than independent observations.
